first.rationale: The onboarding decline is an immediate, broad funnel constraint, and prior evidence indicates simplification produced durable activation and time-to-value gains. I would verify both onboarding records for consistency and the pricing record as the strongest competing response. Promotional pricing may counter the competitor faster, but its effect on customer quality, retention, and post-discount revenue is not established in the consolidated memory, creating downstream-value risk. This intent remains provisional pending archive review.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening the onboarding flow. The directly relevant source showed completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, addressing both current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable revenue. SMB signup simplification provides additional evidence of activation and qualified-revenue lift, though its slight retention decline and limited segment replication warrant guardrails. Reject promotional pricing despite its acquisition lift because retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive first renewal.
